dar

Introduction

dar provides recipe-based differential abundance workflows for microbiome data. It accepts phyloseq and TreeSummarizedExperiment inputs and combines preprocessing, quality control and multiple statistical methods through a common, pipeable interface.

A centralized model defines covariates, contrasts, reference levels and the taxonomic level of analysis. Compatibility checks identify which methods can execute that design. Results can be inspected, visualized and compared in a common format while retaining method-specific effect scales. Native options remain explicit, and recipes can be shared through a versioned, non-executable export format.

Consensus is optional: it summarizes agreement across methods for the same contrast and effect direction. Agreement does not guarantee greater accuracy or false-discovery-rate control, and stricter rules can reduce sensitivity.

Installation

You can install the development version of dar from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("MicrobialGenomics-IrsicaixaOrg/dar")

Usage 

library(dar)
data("metaHIV_phy")

## Define recipe
rec <-
  recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  add_model(
    ~ RiskGroup2,
    targets = "RiskGroup2",
    tax_level = "Species"
  ) |>
  step_subset_taxa(tax_level = "Kingdom", taxa = c("Bacteria", "Archaea")) |>
  step_filter_taxa(.f = "function(x) sum(x > 0) >= (0.03 * length(x))") |>
  step_maaslin() |>
  step_aldex()

rec

## Prep recipe
da_results <- prep(rec, parallel = TRUE)
da_results

## Inspect per-method results in a common format
tidy_results(da_results) |>
  dplyr::select(
    taxa_id, comparison, effect_size, effect_metric,
    adj_p_value, significant, method, step_id
  )

The effect_metric column identifies each method’s effect scale; effect sizes from different methods are not necessarily directly comparable. The per-method results can be used without applying a consensus rule.

Optional consensus summary

To add an agreement-based summary, specify the number of supporting methods with bake() and extract the selected taxa with cool():

n_methods <- 2
da_results <- bake(da_results, count_cutoff = n_methods)
da_results

## Results
cool(da_results)
